key_insight: The paper shows that tiny vision-language models can be made trustworthy and effective for time-series anomaly detection by pairing them with the right supervision and benchmark design. Instead of relying on oversized multimodal models, the approach focuses on efficient, grounded reasoning over sequential data.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between existing anomaly detection benchmarks and the needs of vision-language models: datasets usually provide interval labels but not natural-language explanations, making it hard to train models to produce interpretable, grounded anomaly judgments.
method: Construct a new benchmark, VisAnomBench, that adds natural-language rationales to time-series anomaly data.
Use this benchmark to fine-tune vision-language models so they can reason about abnormal patterns in sequential signals.
Target efficient, smaller models rather than large multimodal systems to improve practicality while maintaining trustworthy outputs.
impact: This matters because it makes AI-based anomaly detection more interpretable and easier to deploy in real-world monitoring settings. Practitioners get a path toward smaller, cheaper models that can explain why they flagged an event as anomalous.

paper_title: Tiny but Trusted: Efficient Vision-Language Reasoning for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Xiaona Zhou, Muntasir Wahed, Tianjiao Yu, Constantin Brif, Ismini Lourentzou
